source_data.title: fluconazole — drug interactions
source_data.content: Fluconazole is a potent inhibitor of CYP2C9 and may increase the anticoagulant effect of warfarin. Concomitant administration of fluconazole and warfarin has been associated with prolonged prothrombin time and elevated INR, increasing the risk of serious bleeding. Prothrombin time should be carefully monitored when fluconazole is co-administered with warfarin and the warfarin dose adjusted as needed.

source_data.title: fluconazole — warnings
source_data.content: Rare cases of serious hepatic injury have been reported with fluconazole. Discontinue fluconazole if clinical signs of liver disease develop. Fluconazole may prolong the QT interval; use caution in patients with proarrhythmic conditions.

source_data.title: warfarin — drug interactions
source_data.content: Many drugs interact with warfarin and may increase the risk of bleeding. Inhibitors of CYP2C9 such as fluconazole can increase warfarin exposure, prolong prothrombin time, and elevate INR. Concomitant use with antifungal agents requires close monitoring of INR.

source_data.title: warfarin — boxed warning
source_data.content: WARNING: BLEEDING RISK. Warfarin can cause major or fatal bleeding. Regular monitoring of INR should be performed on all treated patients.
